$comment: Generated by hack/company-schema.py; platform/product facts come from cd-delivery, pipeline settings from cd-pipeline.
title: cd-project

project.description: Company-owned: the project, its charts, clusters and promotion order.

name.description: The project: the service name of its Applications and, unless the platform names the Kargo Project (pipeline.project.name), its Kargo Project, namespace and Warehouse.

source.description: The project's chart. Optional for a project that releases companions alone (project.companions): its Warehouses subscribe to the companions, its Stages write and check their pins alone, and it installs no chart; adding a source later adds the chart beside them.

chart.description: The application chart, oci://<repository>/<chart>: what the Warehouse subscribes to, and the repository and chart of every ring's Application (<chart>, <chart>-infra, <chart>-e2e).

infraChart.description: The infra chart, released with the application chart and installed at its pin; must be <chart>-infra. Refused for a kind with no infra ring.

versionPrefix.description: Written in front of the version in the pin, for a repository whose tags carry one.

subscribeAs.description: How the Warehouse discovers the chart. `chart` (default) is a chart subscription. `image` is an image subscription with SemVer selection and `strictSemvers: false`, for an OCI chart whose tags carry a `v` (Helm's tag listing drops them, so a chart subscription finds nothing). A leading `oci://` is dropped from `repoURL` for the subscription, the promotion steps write the discovered tag as it is (the `v` stays), and `name` and `versionPrefix` are refused.

kind.description: The kind of product, put into every cluster's product facts: product (default; <chart>, <chart>-infra, <chart>-e2e) or chart (the app ring alone, no infraChart). A static site has no chart for the Warehouse and is not accepted.

sources.description: Further sources of the same product, by name: each one a Warehouse of its own, <project>-<name>, and the repository the clusters that take it (pipeline.stageSources) install every ring from. `kind` and the ring charts are project.source's; the chart name must be the same.

chart.description: oci://<repository>/<chart>, with project.source.chart's <chart>: <chart>-infra and <chart>-e2e come from the same repository. Required with project.source; a project of companions alone names none, and its source is {}.

versionPrefix.description: Written in front of the version in the pin, for a repository whose tags carry one.

subscribeAs.description: How the Warehouse discovers the chart. `chart` (default) is a chart subscription. `image` is an image subscription with SemVer selection and `strictSemvers: false`, for an OCI chart whose tags carry a `v` (Helm's tag listing drops them, so a chart subscription finds nothing). A leading `oci://` is dropped from `repoURL` for the subscription, the promotion steps write the discovered tag as it is (the `v` stays), and `name` and `versionPrefix` are refused.

customers.description: The customers the project is installed for, one Kargo Project for all of them: each one a customer the platform registered (pipeline.project.customers), with a Warehouse of its own, <project>-<customer>, and a chain of Stages along pipeline.stageOrder, named by pipeline.graph.stageName (default <cluster>-<customer>). Each install is keyed by its Stage's name in pins, values and products, is the service <project>-<customer> and runs in that namespace unless the platform's products name another. With project.sources each customer has a Warehouse of each source too, <project>-<customer>-<source>, on its chart from that source, and its install on a cluster whose Stage takes the source (pipeline.stageSources) takes every ring from there.

chart.description: The customer's application chart, oci://<repository>/<chart>, in place of project.source.chart: its Warehouse subscribes to it and its installs take every ring from it (<chart>-infra where project.source has an infraChart).

companions.description: This customer's own semver for a companion of project.companions, in its Warehouse alone: to hold one customer to a line of the shared artifact, or to let a fix of an older line reach that customer only.

additionalProperties.description: oci://<repository>/<chart>, the customer's chart from another repository.

sources.description: The customer's chart from each further source of project.sources, by its name, in place of the source's own chart: required for a customer with a chart of its own, since a source gives the same chart from another repository. The source's semver, versionPrefix and subscribeAs hold.

components.description: With project.components (required there): the components this customer takes, each a key of project.components. Each one is an install of its own on each cluster, keyed by its Stage's name (pipeline.graph.stageName, default <cluster>-<customer>-<component>), the service <project>-<customer>-<component>. Not every customer takes every component.

source.description: A source of each component the customer takes (project.components.<component>.sources): the lane's Stages take the Warehouse <warehouse>-<component>-<source>, and its installs every ring from that source's chart.

stage.description: The lane's one cluster: the first Stage of project.pipeline.stageOrder (the default), and no other.

lane.description: With project.components: this customer is a lane, a preview of its components from a further source, named <customer>-<lane> so its Stages, installs and pins are its own. It is installed on the first cluster of project.pipeline.stageOrder alone; its one Stage there takes the components' Warehouses of the source, promotes on its own and promotes nothing onward.

components.description: A product made of several parts, each one a chart of its own, by name: each one a component the platform registered (pipeline.project.components). One Kargo Project delivers them all: each component has one Warehouse, <warehouse>-<component>, shared by every customer that takes it (project.customers[].components), and one of each of its sources, <warehouse>-<component>-<source>, for the lane customers (project.customers[].lane). Not with project.source, project.sources, project.companions or pipeline.stageSources.

source.description: The component's chart, as project.source is a project's: what its Warehouse subscribes to, and the repository and chart of every ring of its installs.

infraChart.description: The component's infra chart; must be <chart>-infra. Refused for a kind with no infra ring.

versionPrefix.description: Written in front of the version in the pin, for a repository whose tags carry one.

subscribeAs.description: How the Warehouse discovers the chart. `chart` (default) is a chart subscription. `image` is an image subscription with SemVer selection and `strictSemvers: false`, for an OCI chart whose tags carry a `v` (Helm's tag listing drops them, so a chart subscription finds nothing). A leading `oci://` is dropped from `repoURL` for the subscription, the promotion steps write the discovered tag as it is (the `v` stays), and `name` and `versionPrefix` are refused.

kind.description: The kind of product of the component's installs: product (default) or chart.

sources.description: The component's further sources, by name: each one a Warehouse <warehouse>-<component>-<source>, which a lane customer naming the source takes.

chart.description: oci://<repository>/<chart>, with the component's <chart>: <chart>-infra and <chart>-e2e come from the same repository.

versionPrefix.description: Written in front of the version in the pin, for a repository whose tags carry one.

subscribeAs.description: How the Warehouse discovers the chart. `chart` (default) is a chart subscription. `image` is an image subscription with SemVer selection and `strictSemvers: false`, for an OCI chart whose tags carry a `v` (Helm's tag listing drops them, so a chart subscription finds nothing). A leading `oci://` is dropped from `repoURL` for the subscription, the promotion steps write the discovered tag as it is (the `v` stays), and `name` and `versionPrefix` are refused.

companions.description: Artifacts released beside the chart and promoted with it in one Freight, by name: today a static bundle served by the platform's static-site chart (kind static-site). Each Warehouse subscribes to the chart and to every companion, and each Stage writes the chart's pin and the companion's digest, <pin key>-<name>, in one commit. Beside each install (a cluster, or a customer's Stage) the companion is an install of its own keyed <key>-<name> in pins, values and products, the service <service>-<name> in the install's namespace; the platform's products.<key>-<name> give its chartVersion and platformValues.

artifact.description: The artifact's repository, <registry>/<path>, without a tag or digest: what the Warehouse subscribes to and the static-site chart serves at the pinned digest.

kind.description: The kind of the companion's install: static-site (default and only).

artifact.description: The artifact's repository in that source, <registry>/<path>, without a tag or digest.

semver.description: The range of the artifact from that source; default the companion's semver.

sources.description: The companion from a further source of project.sources, by its name: the Warehouses of that source subscribe to this artifact in place of the companion's, and an install on a cluster whose Stage takes the source (pipeline.stageSources) serves it. A source not named here gives the companion's own artifact.

clusters.description: The clusters the project runs on; each one the platform registered (clusters).

stageOrder.description: The Stages, in order; each one a cluster of project.clusters whose pin it writes.

autoPromote.description: Stages that promote on their own although they have an upstream.

noAutoPromote.description: Stages that do not promote on their own, over autoPromote and over the rule that a Stage with no upstream does. The platform may hold back more (pipeline.project.noAutoPromote).

noPrereleases.description: Stages that take releases only: their promotion refuses a version with a prerelease part (1.4.0-rc.1), for the chart and for each companion. For the Stage that must never run a release candidate an earlier Stage ran. The platform may name more (pipeline.project.noPrereleases).

upstreams.description: Replaces pipeline.graph.upstreams for the Stages it names.

stageSources.description: Stage -> a key of project.sources: the Warehouse the Stage takes Freight from and the repository its cluster installs from. A Stage it does not name takes project.source. A Stage and its upstream take the same source; an empty upstreams entry takes Freight straight from the Warehouse.

values.description: Company-owned ring payloads per cluster of project.clusters (per Stage, <cluster>-<customer>, with project.customers), held to cd-company's ownership rules.

pins.description: Company-owned (Kargo writes them): the version per cluster of project.clusters (per Stage with project.customers); an empty string is dormant, and so is a cluster (or Stage) with no key.

clusters.description: Platform-owned: the clusters the platform registered for this project.

clusterName.description: The destination cluster's name in Argo CD, and the {cluster} token in every template below.

argocdNamespace.description: The namespace the Applications are created in.

applicationSuffixes.description: The suffix of each ring's Application NAME (infra, app, e2e); default -infra, none, -e2e. The chart, repository and release keep their names.

applicationPrefix.description: Prepended to every Application's name (empty is allowed); accepts {vendor}, {customer} and {component} where the platform gives them.

appProject.description: The AppProject every Application runs under, with {product} and {cluster} tokens and, where the platform gives them, {vendor}, {customer} and {component}.

vendor.description: Who makes the products of this installation: the {vendor} token of appProject, applicationPrefix and applicationLabels. One of them naming {vendor} without it is refused.

customer.description: Whom this installation is for: the {customer} token, as vendor.

component.description: Which part of a product made of several (each its own chart) this installation is: the {component} token, as vendor.

applicationLabels.description: Labels on every Application; values accept the {product} and {cluster} tokens and, where the platform gives them, {vendor}, {customer} and {component}.

waves.description: Deprecated and ignored: Applications carry no sync-wave. Accepted for one release so a consumer can drop it.

chartRegistry.description: Base reference the charts are published under, used for a product that names no repository of its own.

availability.description: The cluster's redundancy, passed to the application chart as `availability` from delivery interface 14, which sizes its replicas and disruption budget from it. Unset: nothing is passed (the chart's default, single).

finalizer.description: Add the Argo CD resources finalizer, so removing an Application removes what it deployed.

revisionHistoryLimit.description: spec.revisionHistoryLimit of every Application: how many past syncs it keeps in status.history. Each entry holds the sources' valuesObject inline, so the more it keeps the larger the object; Argo CD's own default of 10 can make an Application too large for etcd to accept. Default 3.

syncRetry.description: Retry policy of every generated Application except the end-to-end one, which never retries. Defaults: no limit, refresh on each retry so it resolves the latest revision, backoff 15s doubling to 5m.

iamNameTemplate.description: Name of a product's cloud role, with {cluster}, {slug} and {product} tokens. At most 64 characters once filled.

bucketNameTemplate.description: Name of a product's bucket, with the same tokens.

cloud.description: The cloud facts, needed by a product that has a bucketSlug.

labels.description: Labels the database carries; values accept {product} and {cluster}.

account.description: The broker account of a product, with {product} and {cluster} tokens.

tls.description: Present only where the broker accepts a workload identity.

database.description: The root a database client verifies the server against.

identity.description: Needed by a product with workloadIdentity.

ignoreDifferences.description: ignoreDifferences entries the application ring of every product whose alerts reach its chart (`alerts.enabled`, interface 12 or higher) gets first, for a rule kind whose live object carries server-side defaults the render does not.

alerts.description: What the platform adds for a product's alert rules.

dashboards.description: Passed to the application ring as `observability.dashboards`, verbatim, for every product with `dashboards: true` (the folder and data sources of this cluster's dashboards). Unset: nothing is passed.

infraLabels.description: Labels the infrastructure Application of every `static-site` product gets, verbatim. Ordering that must hold between the two Applications of a site (a sync gate, say) is the platform's, and is handed through here; the chart names none. Unset: none.

siteAnnotations.description: Annotations the site Application of every `static-site` product gets, verbatim (a sync wave, say). Unset: none.

staticSite.description: What the platform adds to the Applications of a `static-site` product.

platform.description: Platform-owned: cd-company's platform block, per cluster.

interface.description: The highest delivery interface the pinned charts read (truvity/policy docs/contracts/delivery-interface.md).

parentRef.description: The route's parent, passed by name.

runtimeRole.description: Defaults to true: the infra chart is handed postgres.runtimeRole, runtimePasswordSecret and runtimePassword.generate. Set false for an infra chart whose postgres schema does not have them; none of the three is sent. Refused at delivery interface 15 or higher, where the runtime role is not optional.

migrations.description: The product declares that it runs schema migrations. From delivery interface 15 the owner's credential is then passed to the application chart as database.migration.passwordSecret, for a migration Job or hook Job alone; the long-running workloads get database.app.* only, always. Unset: no owner credential is passed at 15 or higher. Refused below 15, where the owner credential is passed as database.owner.passwordSecret.

kargoStage.description: `<kargo project>:<stage>` that may sync the end-to-end Application. Rendered as the `kargo.akuity.io/authorized-stage` annotation on that Application only; omitted when unset.

sync.description: `auto` (default): the end-to-end Application syncs by itself. `manual`: it renders without `syncPolicy.automated`, for a Kargo Stage that syncs it.

hook.description: Render the end-to-end suite's Job as an Argo CD Sync hook (hook-delete-policy BeforeHookCreation, sync-wave 1) instead of a tracked resource with Force and Replace. Default false.

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description: Seconds a finished hook Job is kept, when `hook` is true. Default 86400; the end-to-end chart refuses less than 120.

alerts.description: The product's alert values (enabled, remote, ruleLabels, alertLabels, one block of thresholds per rule), passed to the application chart verbatim from interface 12.

dashboards.description: The product's chart renders dashboards: it is handed `platform.dashboards` as `observability.dashboards` where the platform states one.

platformValues.description: The platform's own payload per ring, merged over what the chart composed and before `layers` and `values`. In `cd-company` it is platform-owned: a company cannot override a path it sets.

name.description: The layer's name, unique in the product.

since.description: The first release whose chart reads these values, `x.y.z`. The layer applies when the product's `pin` (a leading `v` is ignored) is at or above it, counting a prerelease of it (`>=since-0`); a pin that is not a version turns it off.

required.description: With `true`, a pin below `since` is a render failure instead of a silent skip.

values.description: Merged like `platformValues`, when the layer's pin gate is open.

layers.description: Ordered, pin-gated payloads owned by the platform: a chart's closed schema rejects a key an older release does not read, and the pin moves without the platform rendering anything, so the comparison is made here. Merged after `platformValues` in list order, before `values`.

namespace.description: The destination namespace (default the product's name). A product of kind `product` that names one keeps its name for its release, its Helm objects and its pins: one install of a product in its own namespace.

applicationName.description: Kinds `product` and `static-site`: the middle of the product's Application names (default the product's name). Installs of one product for several customers name it alike and take the customer in `platform.applicationPrefix` (`{customer}`).

vendor.description: Kinds `product` and `static-site`: this product's `{vendor}` in the platform's name patterns, over `platform.vendor`.

customer.description: Kinds `product` and `static-site`: this product's `{customer}` in the platform's name patterns, over `platform.customer`: one install of a product for one customer.

component.description: Kinds `product` and `static-site`: this product's `{component}` in the platform's name patterns, over `platform.component`: one part of a product made of several, beside the others in the same call.

chartVersion.description: Kind `static-site` only: the release of the `static-site` and `static-site-infra` charts, the targetRevision of both Applications.

ref.description: The repository of the site artifact, without a tag or digest. The chart is given this and `pin`.

products.description: Platform-owned: the project's product facts, per cluster (per Stage with project.customers; cd-company's products.<service>).

pipeline.description: Platform-owned: the allowlisted cd-pipeline settings. No credentials, verification, access, Project or AppProjects.

labels.description: Labels on every object. None by default: the chart adds nothing the values do not say.

annotations.description: Annotations on every object, beside the sync-wave. None by default.

waves.description: The Argo CD sync-wave of each kind of object.

namespace.description: Where the Argo CD Applications of the Stages live.

repoURL.description: The repository a promotion writes the pin to.

git.description: The repository a promotion writes the pin to. The write-back credentials are the platform's and are not rendered here.

pinFile.description: The file the pin is written to, relative to the repository; tokens {stage}, {project}, {slug}, {product} (the slug), {pinKey} and, where the project gives them, {vendor} and {customer}.

pinKey.description: The key written in it; the same tokens.

commitMessage.description: The same tokens and {version}, the Kargo expression for the promoted version.

seedPinFile.description: Seed a missing pin file: before yaml-update, a file-write step (alias seed-pin, overwrite false, continueOnError true) writes the pin file with every key this Stage writes, each "" (dormant), so a Stage's first promotion into a folder with no pin file succeeds. An existing file is never changed: on every later promotion the step fails with "already exists", which continueOnError ignores, and the Promotion succeeds. It adds no key to an existing file. Default false.

jobs.description: What every verification Job is run as.

upstreams.description: Stage -> the Stages it may promote from, in preference; the first the project has wins.

applicationName.description: The Argo CD Application a derived Stage watches; tokens {stage}, {app}, {project}, {slug}, {product} (the slug) and, where the project gives them, {vendor} and {customer}.

promotedVersion.description: Every derived Stage runs the promoted-version check.

stageName.description: The name of a Stage of a customer's chain (`projects[].customers`), with the tokens `{stage}` (the Stage of `stageOrder`), `{customer}` and, with `projects[].components`, `{component}`; default `{stage}-{customer}`, or `{stage}-{customer}-{component}` with components.

graph.description: The promotion graph: with promotedVersion every derived Stage names the promoted-version check, whose objects are the platform's and never rendered here; no access subjects here.

project.description: What the platform says about this project's Kargo Project. Read by cd-project itself, not a cd-pipeline setting; sealed with the rest of pipeline, so a company file cannot set it.

name.description: The Kargo Project, and so the namespace of the Warehouse, Stages and ProjectConfig (and, by default, the Warehouse's name); tokens {project} and {product} (project.name), {vendor}, {customer}. Unset, it is project.name. With it project.name is the slug: Application names, the pin key and check names stay. A Kargo Project cannot be renamed: a new name is a new Project with a new Freight history.

installName.description: The middle of the Application names of a customer's install, with project.customers: tokens {project} (project.name), {customer}, {component} (with project.components, where it is required) and {vendor} (where pipeline.project sets it); a companion's is <installName>-<companion>. Default {project}, the customer then in the platform's applicationPrefix. With {project}-{customer} and the prefix <cluster>-, the Applications are <cluster>-<project>-<customer>-<ring suffix>. The Stages watch the same names.

warehouse.description: The name of the project's Warehouse, as given: the product, or <product>-<customer> for a product built for each customer. A further source's Warehouse is <warehouse>-<source>, a customer's <warehouse>-<customer>. Unset, project.name. A Warehouse cannot be renamed in place: a new name is a new Warehouse, and its Freight starts again.

vendor.description: Who makes the product: the {vendor} token of name, promotion.pinFile, pinKey, commitMessage, prTitle and graph.applicationName.

customer.description: Whom this installation is for: the {customer} token, as vendor.

semver.description: The platform's range of the project's chart: every Warehouse of the project (project.source, each source, each customer) subscribes within it, the company's range AND this one, and a pin outside it is refused. For a floor below which the platform cannot install the chart, or a ceiling it has not prepared for. Unset, the company's range alone.

customers.description: The customers the platform registered for this product, each one an installation of its own: project.customers may name only these. Not with customer: a product with several customers has one Kargo Project, cd-<vendor>-<project>, and {customer} is each Stage's own.

components.description: The components the platform registered for this product, each a chart of its own: project.components may name only these, and needs them. With them the default pipeline.graph.stageName is {stage}-{customer}-{component} and installName {project}-{customer}-{component}; an installName must name {component}.

metricsGateStages.description: Stages of project.pipeline.stageOrder that run the platform's metrics gate after a promotion: each names `<slug>-<stage>-metrics-gate` in its verification, and the gate's ServiceAccount, ConfigMap and AnalysisTemplate are the platform's (rendered where the gate runs, never here).

noAutoPromote.description: Stages the platform holds back from promoting on their own, beside project.pipeline.noAutoPromote: to quiesce a pipeline while it is moved, so that one Kargo Project writes a pin.

noPrereleases.description: Stages the platform keeps prereleases out of, beside project.pipeline.noPrereleases: their promotion refuses a version with a prerelease part.

stages.description: A project split across two releases while it moves cluster by cluster: the leading Stages of project.pipeline.stageOrder this release renders, Applications and Stages, and no other. The company's lists are narrowed to them, a further source none of them takes is left out, and a kept Stage whose upstream is left out is refused. Not with handedOver, customers or companions.

handedOver.description: The other part of a split project: clusters of project.clusters whose Applications another release renders. This release renders none for them and needs no platform facts for them; their Stages stay and are held, so one Kargo Project writes each pin. Not with stages, customers or companions.

platformDigest.description: Platform-owned: sha256 of toJson of {clusters, pipeline, platform, products} as the platform passes them.

global.description: Helm's own: a parent chart's global values reach every subchart. The chart reads none of it.
